newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran president-elect says better ties up to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Iran president-elect says better ties up to U.S.

text.p: Iranian president-elect Mohammad Khatami said on Tuesday any improvement in relations between the Islamic republic and the United States depended on Washington changing its hostile policies towards Tehran.
Khatami, a moderate former culture minister who won a landslide victory in last Friday's polls, told his first news conference he did not see any changes in U.S. policy.
"We are sorry to see that the United States policy has always been...hostile to our revolution," he told Iranian and foreign journalists.

"We cannot accept domineering...policies. Any change in relations with the United States depends on changes in the policies of America towards the revolution and Iran, and unfortunately we do not see any sign of such change in American policy," said Khatami, speaking through an interpreter.
"In regard to relations with the United States of America, I should say that America is the source...of this problem," he said.
Khatami said "there will be no ground for any relations" between the two countries as long as the United States wanted to harm Iranian independence and national interest.

"The great outcome of our revolution is independence and we are not willing to give up this valuable outcome we have gained. The basis of our relations with other countries relies on the independence and national interest of our country," he said.

Iran has repeatedly denied U.S. accusations it supports international terrorism and was developing nuclear weapons. Iranian leaders had said any breakthrough in relations with the United States depended on a change in U.S. policy.

The United States -- which has imposed sanctions on Iran in an effort to isolate it -- has said it is closely watching the aftermath of Iran's elections to see if there were changes in the country's behaviour.
Khatami takes over as president in August.
